Final-position-only loss is not required by GRU4Rec. The original training procedure predicts successive next events throughout each session, using sampled output candidates. Dense causal supervision therefore fits the family, although full-sequence backpropagation differs from its original session-parallel updates. Random-prefix final-position training can also cover intermediate targets across repeated draws; coverage depends on endpoint probabilities and truncation. Recency sampling research explicitly studies this choice and reports improved accuracy/training efficiency for GRU4Rec and other sequential models. ([GRU4Rec paper](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=ryCM8zWRb), [recency sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643))

Experimental implications, derived from these objectives: dense loss reuses a GRU forward pass for multiple targets but increases scoring/backward work; final-only loss scores fewer targets while potentially recomputing overlapping prefixes. Normalize dense loss over valid targets, excluding padding. A global target mean weights longer histories more than averaging each history’s loss first; uniform-user, uniform-prefix sampling induces another weighting. Keep negative distribution, exclusions, count per target and loss reduction fixed. Changing to in-batch negatives also changes the candidate distribution; the official implementation documents both batch-derived negatives and additional sampled negatives. ([GRU4Rec implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec))

For a clean causal suffix-cropping ablation, first choose a training target, then remove only older items from its preceding context, preserving order and the immediate predecessor. Keep the target and its negative candidates unchanged; exclude the target and subsequent events from that input. This tests context truncation separately from target resampling. Dense supervision plus random endpoints can repeatedly weight overlapping transitions, so report target exposures and elapsed training time alongside updates. With left padding, final-only readout must select the final nonpadding position.
